characteristic_sites: stomach (H. pylori-associated — H. pylori eradication first-line)

biomarkers.name: H. pylori (gastric MALT)
biomarkers.clinical_use: H. pylori eradication is first-line — induces lymphoma remission in most H. pylori+ localized disease

biomarkers.name: t(11;18)(q21;q21) BIRC3-MALT1
biomarkers.prevalence: ~20–30% overall in gastric MALT; enriched in H. pylori-resistant cases
biomarkers.clinical_use: Predicts poor response / failure of H. pylori eradication and relative lack of response to alkylating-agent monotherapy — local therapy (e.g. RT) or rituximab-based systemic therapy is generally preferred when treatment is needed

biomarkers.name: t(14;18)(q32;q21) IGH-MALT1
biomarkers.prevalence: Seen in a subset of nongastric MALT, including ocular adnexa, salivary gland, skin, and liver; uncommon in gastric MALT
biomarkers.clinical_use: Recurrent MALT lymphoma translocation with site enrichment

biomarkers.name: t(3;14)(p14.1;q32) IGH-FOXP1
biomarkers.prevalence: Uncommon; reported in subsets of thyroid and ocular adnexal MALT and other extranodal sites

biomarkers.name: Chlamydia psittaci (ocular adnexa)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Doxycycline may induce remission in some ocular adnexal MALT cases; predictive value remains inconsistent/contested

biomarkers.name: Autoimmune disease association (Sjögren for salivary, Hashimoto for thyroid)
MYD88 L265P (usually negative)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Helps distinguish from lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenström macroglobulinemia

biomarkers.name: t(1;14)(p22;q32) / IGH-BCL10 and t(1;2)(p22;p12) BCL10-IGK
biomarkers.clinical_use: Hallmark recurrent MALT lymphoma rearrangements leading to NF-κB pathway activation

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Small B lymphocytes with plasmacytic differentiation infiltrating epithelium and forming lymphoepithelial lesions in mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Chronic antigen-driven — H. pylori (gastric), Chlamydia psittaci (ocular, variably supported geographically), Borrelia burgdorferi (some cutaneous cases in endemic regions), Sjögren autoimmunity (salivary), Hashimoto (thyroid); antigen removal can induce regression in selected infection-driven forms
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Lymphoepithelial lesions (lymphocytes invading epithelium) are characteristic; reactive follicles may be retained

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Post-germinal-center marginal zone B cells recruited to mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) through chronic antigen exposure
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Mesoderm — lymphoid (marginal zone B cells at mucosal sites)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Marginal zone B-cell differentiation with plasmacytic differentiation; forms lymphoepithelial lesions (lymphocytes invading epithelium) — characteristic feature; retains marginal zone immunophenotype
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Chronic antigen-driven clonal evolution — site-specific antigens drive characteristic MALT lymphomas: H. pylori (gastric), Chlamydia psittaci (ocular, variably supported), Borrelia burgdorferi (cutaneous in some endemic regions), Sjögren autoimmunity (salivary), Hashimoto (thyroid); antigen removal can induce regression in selected cases; transformation to DLBCL represents progression with additional genetic events
